basis: Congenital multiple joint contractures with muscle weakness/fibrosis define this umbrella; neurologic causes vary across subtypes.
Severe bone fragility and prenatal fractures define OI8; global developmental delay reported in 1/2 patients supports neurologic involvement, with limited frequency evidence.
Limb dysostosis and severe intellectual disability define it; cleft palate and eyelid coloboma each 80-99%; anonychia and skin abnormalities omitted by cap.
Tumor arises in reproductive organs; resemblance to transitional epithelium does not establish urinary tract origin.
Congenital atrial septal defect; associated conduction abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis.
Chronic congestive enlargement of the spleen; underlying hepatic or cardiovascular causes are separate conditions.
Developmental impairment is shared across major 6p deletion syndromes; ocular and other malformations depend on deletion extent and are not established across the umbrella.
Developmental encephalopathy defines it; visual impairment in 9/10 supports ocular functional loss, though localization is unspecified; constipation alone does not establish gut damage.
Necrotizing lesion of minor salivary glands; local ischemic inflammation does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.
Cerebral palsy affecting motor control of one limb; spasticity does not establish a separate intrinsic muscle disorder.
Defined as a cutaneous dermoid neoplasm; possible swallowing or airway compression does not establish common direct gastrointestinal or pulmonary damage.
Inherited biochemical disorder with urinary excretion of diaminopentane (cadaverine); abnormal urinary metabolites alone do not establish renal damage.
Glioma originates in the optic nerve, explicitly included in the ocular axis; associated NF1 is a separate disease.
Hereditary amyloid deposition with defining gut dysfunction; autonomic neuropathy is defining and median neuropathy 30-79%; renal amyloidosis/CKD 30-79%; cardiac/hepatic disease 5-29%.
Cerebellar hypoplasia, ataxia and intellectual disability define it; persistent strabismus in 4/4; pes planus in 4/4 does not alone establish damaging skeletal dysfunction.
Neurodevelopmental impairment, hypogonadism and skeletal malformations are core; dental enamel defects 80-99%; renal, ocular and ear abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap.
Developmental impairment is central; myopia/amblyopia 30-79%; listed renal and specific skeletal defects mostly 5-29%; pilomatrixoma is a separate associated tumor.
Meningioma arises in the meninges of the central nervous system.
Benign neoplasm of the uterine corpus or cervix; reproductive organs have no axis.
Congenital absence of part of an eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Motor neuron degeneration, sometimes with frontotemporal dementia; weakness and dysphagia reflect neurologic injury rather than separate muscle or gut disease.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no other organ disease is established.
Microcephaly and motor developmental delay occur in 30-79%; specific cardiac, ocular, intestinal and skeletal malformations are mostly 5-29%; unspecified hernia adds no clear organ damage.
Ciguatoxin poisoning is defined by neurologic, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular toxic dysfunction; toxin ingestion is not an infection.
Carcinoma originates in the axillary tail of the breast; breast has no axis.
